sourcedFrom: Kahr® Semi-Auto Double Action Only (DAO) Pistols — Operating Instructions — 12195KMM (code printed on the back cover; the file name reads 1295KMM) (2019 (back cover: "© 2019, Kahr Firearms Group"))
cleanIntro: A double-action-only polymer 9mm that field strips into its main components: line the witness marks up, push the slide stop out from right to left, release the striker, and run the slide off the front. Kahr's book stops there for the pistol and says so, and Deep Clean follows it only as far as it goes — the magazine, down to its spring and follower.

steps.title: Magazine out first
steps.action: Point the pistol in a safe direction and keep your finger out of the trigger guard. Press the magazine catch on the front of the left grip and pull the magazine out of the well.
steps.prose: The CM9 has no manual safety and no magazine disconnect, so a round left in the chamber will fire whether the magazine is in or out — Kahr says so in its own warnings. That is why the magazine comes out before anything else moves: with it seated, working the slide only feeds a fresh round. Put it down away from the bench.
steps.quote: Remove the Magazine by depressing the Magazine Catch on the front of the left grip
steps.cite: Kahr® Semi-Auto Double Action Only (DAO) Pistols — Operating Instructions — 12195KMM (code printed on the back cover; the file name reads 1295KMM) — Unloading, p.17

steps.title: Rack the chamber empty
steps.action: With the magazine out, pull the slide fully to the rear to throw out any round that may be in the chamber.
steps.prose: One full stroke all the way back: a short pull can draw a cartridge part way and let it drop back into the chamber. The slide is short and stiff on a gun this size, so get a firm grip on the serrations rather than pinching the rear. Keep your fingers clear of the ejection port while you do it.
steps.quote: Pull the Slide fully to the rear to eject the round which may be in the chamber.
steps.cite: Kahr® Semi-Auto Double Action Only (DAO) Pistols — Operating Instructions — 12195KMM (code printed on the back cover; the file name reads 1295KMM) — Unloading, p.17

steps.title: Look, and see it empty for yourself
steps.action: Hold the slide back and look into the chamber and down the magazine well. Both must be empty. Then let the slide go forward.
steps.prose: Kahr puts this one in red: you have to see the empty chamber yourself, because a later step presses the trigger. Nothing on the CM9 tells you it is loaded — the loaded chamber indicator in this book belongs to a different Kahr model. If you are not sure what you saw, rack and look again.
steps.quote: You must personally verify that the chamber is empty before field-stripping the firearm for cleaning or any other reason.
steps.cite: Kahr® Semi-Auto Double Action Only (DAO) Pistols — Operating Instructions — 12195KMM (code printed on the back cover; the file name reads 1295KMM) — Important Safety Information, p.8

steps.title: Witness marks lined up
steps.action: Draw the slide back about half an inch until the small witness mark on the slide lines up with the one on the frame. Through the rear half-moon cutout in the side of the slide you should see the inside projection of the slide stop.
steps.prose: This is the only position where the slide stop can come out, and it is a narrow one. The marks are small, so tilt the pistol to the light rather than guessing. Hold the slide there with your support hand for the next step; if it slips forward the stop will not move.
steps.quote: Draw the Slide back about 1⁄2 inch so that the small witness marks on the Slide and Frame align
steps.cite: Kahr® Semi-Auto Double Action Only (DAO) Pistols — Operating Instructions — 12195KMM (code printed on the back cover; the file name reads 1295KMM) — Disassembly, step 2, p.18

steps.title: Slide stop pin out, right to left
steps.action: Holding the slide on the marks, push the pin of the slide stop out of the pistol from the right side towards the left, and lift the slide stop away.
steps.prose: The pin end shows on the right of the frame above the trigger. Firm thumb pressure is usually enough on a pistol that has been cleaned; a tight one can be tapped, and Kahr names a light non-marring hammer or a plastic screwdriver handle for that, never a steel punch on the polymer. If it will not start, re-check the witness marks before pushing harder.
steps.quote: Push the pin of the Slide Stop out of the pistol from right to left.
steps.cite: Kahr® Semi-Auto Double Action Only (DAO) Pistols — Operating Instructions — 12195KMM (code printed on the back cover; the file name reads 1295KMM) — Disassembly, step 3, p.18

steps.title: Ease the slide forward
steps.action: Let the slide come forward under your hand on the recoil spring's push. Do not let it snap.
steps.prose: With the slide stop out, nothing is holding the slide on the frame but your grip and the striker, and the recoil spring is still pushing. Letting it ride forward under control keeps it from jumping the rails before you are ready. It will stop short of coming off; that is the striker, and the next step deals with it.
steps.quote: Ease the Slide forward under Recoil Spring tension.
steps.cite: Kahr® Semi-Auto Double Action Only (DAO) Pistols — Operating Instructions — 12195KMM (code printed on the back cover; the file name reads 1295KMM) — Disassembly, step 4, p.18

steps.title: Trigger pulled, slide forward off the frame
steps.action: Check once more that the chamber is empty. Then, muzzle in a safe direction, pull the trigger to release the striker and keep it pulled while you push the slide forward off the frame.
steps.prose: This is the step the empty-chamber check was for. The trigger has to stay held back the whole way, or the cocking cam catches the striker again and the slide stops dead. A slide that will not move with the trigger held is a sign the slide stop is still partly in, not a reason to force it.
steps.quote: while keeping the trigger pulled, push the Slide forward off of the Frame.
steps.cite: Kahr® Semi-Auto Double Action Only (DAO) Pistols — Operating Instructions — 12195KMM (code printed on the back cover; the file name reads 1295KMM) — Disassembly, step 5, p.18
steps.warn: RECOIL SPRING GUIDE IS UNDER TENSION AND MAY FLY OFF AND CAUSE INJURY!

steps.title: Recoil spring assembly out — in one piece
steps.action: Turn the slide over and carefully lift the recoil spring assembly out of the slide. On the CM9 the spring and guide rod come out together as one assembly; leave it that way.
steps.prose: Eyes away from the slide here: the assembly is still loaded against the barrel lug and can jump when it clears. On the CM series the spring and guide are a factory-assembled part that works one way only, and Kahr forbids taking it apart. Set it down whole and note which end faced the barrel.
steps.quote: Carefully remove Recoil Spring Guide with Recoil Spring from Slide.
steps.cite: Kahr® Semi-Auto Double Action Only (DAO) Pistols — Operating Instructions — 12195KMM (code printed on the back cover; the file name reads 1295KMM) — Disassembly, step 6, p.18
steps.warn: DO NOT ATTEMPT TO DISASSEMBLE THE RECOIL SPRING ASSEMBLY FOR MK, PM, AND CM MODELS. THIS IS A FACTORY ASSEMBLED COMPONENT.

steps.title: Barrel out by its lug
steps.action: Take hold of the barrel's recoil lug, push it slightly forward, then lift it and pull it rearward out of the slide.
steps.prose: The lug is the block under the chamber with the kidney-shaped cutout the slide stop runs through. Forward first frees the chamber hood from the slide; lifting before that just jams it. Hold it by the lug rather than the muzzle, and the barrel comes out cleanly backwards.
steps.quote: Grasp recoil lug of Barrel and push it slightly forward, then lift and pull it rearward out of the Slide.
steps.cite: Kahr® Semi-Auto Double Action Only (DAO) Pistols — Operating Instructions — 12195KMM (code printed on the back cover; the file name reads 1295KMM) — Disassembly, step 6, p.19

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: On the bench: the slide, the barrel, the frame, the magazine, the slide stop and the recoil spring assembly. That is the whole of Kahr's field strip, and the pistol comes apart no further than this for cleaning.
steps.prose: Everything the cleaning section names is now in reach: the bore, the slide and its rail grooves, the frame's guide rails, and the lube points on the barrel lug, guide rod and slide stop. Kahr warns that going past the main components can make the pistol unsafe and affect its warranty. Deep Clean covers the one thing the book does take further — the magazine.
steps.quote: For normal cleaning, the KAHR® Pistol should only be disassembled into its main components:
steps.cite: Kahr® Semi-Auto Double Action Only (DAO) Pistols — Operating Instructions — 12195KMM (code printed on the back cover; the file name reads 1295KMM) — Disassembly & Reassembly, p.17
steps.warn: DO NOT DISASSEMBLE THE PISTOL FURTHER THAN THE MAIN COMPONENTS DESCRIBED ABOVE (except Magazine).

deepSteps.title: Magazine: pin through the sight holes
deepSteps.action: Make sure the magazine is empty. Push a 1/8-inch or smaller pin, or a length of stiff wire, through the bottom sight holes of the magazine tube so it passes between the coils of the spring.
deepSteps.prose: The pin holds most of the spring's load while the base comes off, so the spring cannot launch the base or the follower. Pick the lowest pair of holes and make sure the pin goes right across, through both walls. Kahr asks for eye protection for the whole job.
deepSteps.quote: Insert a 1/8” or smaller pin (or length of stiff wire, etc.) through the bottom sight holes in the Magazine Tube (A), between coils of the Magazine Spring (D).
deepSteps.cite: Kahr® Semi-Auto Double Action Only (DAO) Pistols — Operating Instructions — 12195KMM (code printed on the back cover; the file name reads 1295KMM) — Magazine Disassembly, p.22
deepSteps.warn: CAUTION! THE MAGAZINE SPRING IS UNDER PRESSURE.

deepSteps.title: Press the base lock through the base
deepSteps.action: With a small punch, a ball-point pen or similar, press the locking stud of the magazine base lock through the hole in the bottom of the magazine base.
deepSteps.prose: The stud is what keeps the base on the rails; pressing it frees the base to slide. With the pin in, there is little pressure on it and it goes down easily. If it fights you, the pin has probably missed the coils.
deepSteps.quote: depress the locking stud of the Magazine Base Lock (B) through the hole in the bottom of the Magazine Base (C)
deepSteps.cite: Kahr® Semi-Auto Double Action Only (DAO) Pistols — Operating Instructions — 12195KMM (code printed on the back cover; the file name reads 1295KMM) — Magazine Disassembly, p.22

deepSteps.title: Base off, forward
deepSteps.action: Keep the stud pressed and push the magazine base forward off the tube.
deepSteps.prose: The base runs on rails at the bottom of the tube and comes off towards the front of the magazine. It should slide without force once the stud is clear of its hole. The spring now sits on the pin, still under some compression.
deepSteps.quote: Push the Magazine Base forward off the Magazine Tube.
deepSteps.cite: Kahr® Semi-Auto Double Action Only (DAO) Pistols — Operating Instructions — 12195KMM (code printed on the back cover; the file name reads 1295KMM) — Magazine Disassembly, p.22

deepSteps.title: Thumb on the spring, pin out
deepSteps.action: Point the bottom of the tube in a safe direction, hold the free end of the spring with your thumb, and carefully withdraw the pin from the sight holes.
deepSteps.prose: The spring is still compressed, and the moment the pin comes out it pushes against your thumb. Let it rise slowly under the thumb rather than lifting your hand away. The base lock rides on the end of the spring, so keep track of it too.
deepSteps.quote: carefully withdraw the pin from the Magazine sight holes.
deepSteps.cite: Kahr® Semi-Auto Double Action Only (DAO) Pistols — Operating Instructions — 12195KMM (code printed on the back cover; the file name reads 1295KMM) — Magazine Disassembly, p.22

deepSteps.title: Spring and follower out the bottom
deepSteps.action: Take the magazine spring and the follower out through the bottom of the tube. That is as far as the magazine comes apart.
deepSteps.prose: Note which way the follower faced in the tube before you set it down, because it goes back in from the bottom the same way. The tube, spring, follower, base lock and base are the five pieces; nothing else on the magazine is meant to come off.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the Magazine Spring and Magazine Follower (E) through the bottom of the Magazine Tube
deepSteps.cite: Kahr® Semi-Auto Double Action Only (DAO) Pistols — Operating Instructions — 12195KMM (code printed on the back cover; the file name reads 1295KMM) — Magazine Disassembly, p.22

deepSteps.title: Clean, and only a light wipe of oil
deepSteps.action: Clean every magazine part thoroughly with solvent, then wipe them lightly with a cloth moistened with lubricant before you put the magazine back together.
deepSteps.prose: A wipe, not a coat: oil left inside a magazine reaches the cartridges, and Kahr warns it can soak into a primer and cause a failure to fire. Grit inside the tube is what makes the follower drag, so the inside is where the solvent earns its keep.
deepSteps.quote: The Magazine is now completely disassembled. Clean all parts thoroughly with solvent.
deepSteps.cite: Kahr® Semi-Auto Double Action Only (DAO) Pistols — Operating Instructions — 12195KMM (code printed on the back cover; the file name reads 1295KMM) — Magazine Maintenance, p.22

deepSteps.title: Inspect it, and replace what is damaged
deepSteps.action: Check the base and base lock for cracks, the tube for cracks or voids along the seam weld, and the follower for chips and cracks. The follower must move freely in the tube. Look over the feed lips for distortion, burrs or nicks, especially where the magazine catch slot is.
deepSteps.prose: A magazine is the part of the pistol most likely to be dropped, and Kahr is plain about it: a damaged part is replaced, not mended. Bent feed lips are the usual cause of rounds nose-diving or two feeding at once.
deepSteps.quote: Inspect Magazine Follower for chips and cracks.
deepSteps.cite: Kahr® Semi-Auto Double Action Only (DAO) Pistols — Operating Instructions — 12195KMM (code printed on the back cover; the file name reads 1295KMM) — Magazine Maintenance, p.22
deepSteps.warn: Do not attempt to repair it.

deepSteps.title: No further: the rest is Kahr's
deepSteps.action: Do not take the pistol apart beyond its main components. Anything past the field strip and the magazine is factory work.
deepSteps.prose: Kahr warns that disassembly past the main components can create an unsafe condition and affect the warranty, and that a pistol that seems to be working wrongly must be unloaded and not used until Kahr or an authorised gunsmith has repaired and checked it. Kahr's return authorisation form and customer service handle that.
deepSteps.quote: DO NOT DISASSEMBLE THE PISTOL FURTHER THAN THE MAIN COMPONENTS DESCRIBED ABOVE (except Magazine).
deepSteps.cite: Kahr® Semi-Auto Double Action Only (DAO) Pistols — Operating Instructions — 12195KMM (code printed on the back cover; the file name reads 1295KMM) — Disassembly & Reassembly, p.17

cleaning.name: BARREL & BORE
tasks: Clean the inside and outside of the barrel with a commercial gun cleaning solvent
Use only high quality, commercially available cleaning equipment, solvents and lubricants
Kahr does not recommend lead (unjacketed) bullets — they can foul the bore heavily
Lightly coat the whole outside of the barrel tube with lube
Lightly coat the whole inside of the kidney-shaped cutout in the barrel lug

cleaning.name: SLIDE & FRAME
tasks: Remove firing residue from the slide and frame with solvent
Lightly coat the whole outside of the recoil spring guide rod — the assembly stays in one piece
Lightly coat the whole outside of the round part of the slide stop
Slide muzzle straight down, a drop of lube in both rail grooves, and let it run the whole length
Lightly coat the two guide rails on the polymer frame

cleaning.name: HOW OFTEN
tasks: Strip and clean before the first shooting of a new pistol
Repeat the cleaning after every shooting session
Lightly lubricate once a month whether or not it has been fired — lubricants evaporate
Follow the solvent and lubricant makers' own instructions

reassembly: Recoil spring assembly: the smaller closed end of the spring against the flange on the rear of the guide rod, just as it came out — the CM assembly is never taken apart.

Barrel into the slide, then compress the recoil spring assembly between the slide and the barrel lug, parallel to the slide rails and not off to one side, with the large flat disc at the rear of the assembly in front of the barrel's recoil lug.
Line up the kidney-shaped cutout in the barrel lug with the opening in the frame; it may help to line up the back of the slide with the back of the frame first.

Insert the slide stop at the 4 o'clock position about halfway through the frame opening and the cutout, then turn it to 3 o'clock so the slide stop spring catches the top of the landing on the slide stop.
Draw the slide back a quarter inch, confirm the slide stop lines up with the half-moon cutout in the slide, and push the slide stop the rest of the way in.
If the slide will not go smoothly onto the frame, do not force it — take the slide off and recheck the steps above.

Magazine, if you stripped it: follower into the tube from the bottom, then the spring; compress the spring on a hard flat surface and hold it with the pin through the bottom sight holes; press the base lock on the end of the spring and slide the base over it and through the rails on the bottom of the tube.
fncheck: With no ammunition anywhere near the bench: the slide should run smoothly on the frame and the slide stop should sit fully home, not standing proud of the frame on the left. An empty magazine should seat fully when it is inserted — listen for the click and pull down on the base to be sure it is locked — and fall freely from the well when the magazine catch is pressed. If the pistol seems to work wrongly in any way, Kahr's instruction is to unload it and not use it until Kahr or an authorised gunsmith has repaired and checked it.
